Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LabelAId: Just-in-time AI Interventions for Improving Human Labeling Quality and Domain Knowledge in Crowdsourcing Systems (2403.09810v1) · paper method: The 34-participant university/snowball study required consent and paid $30 per hour. Two researchers independently validated all 3,574 participant labels; disagreement on 74 labels was resolved with a third researcher, and resulting validations defined user-label precision.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LabelAId: Just-in-time AI Interventions for Improving Human Labeling Quality and Domain Knowledge in Crowdsourcing Systems (2403.09810v1) · paper method: In the 34-participant between-subjects Project Sidewalk study, the intervention group had higher overall precision by Mann–Whitney U (p≤0.01), while route completion time showed no significant difference (p=0.693; control mean 2,303.3 seconds, intervention 2,801.4 seconds).

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LabelAId: Just-in-time AI Interventions for Improving Human Labeling Quality and Domain Knowledge in Crowdsourcing Systems (2403.09810v1) · paper method: The implementation could infer likely mistakes but not their exact source and exposed neither explainability features nor global accuracy differences across label types; the authors also caution that the 34-person university/snowball sample may not represent Project Sidewalk’s broader user base.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

LabelAId: Just-in-time AI Interventions for Improving Human Labeling Quality and Domain Knowledge in Crowdsourcing Systems (2403.09810v1) · paper method: LabelAId combines domain-coded labeling functions through a Snorkel probabilistic label model to infer image-label correctness, then pretrains an FT-Transformer before fine-tuning on expert-validated city labels; the proof of concept uses urban-accessibility imagery rather than a general-purpose annotation workload.
